discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in `1544b995b`. `suggestion()` in `candidates.ts` now clips `prompt` to `PROMPT_MAX_CHARS` and `why` to `WHY_MAX_CHARS` before it hashes the id, so rule, model and turn rows all stay inside the published bounds. Text within the limits is unchanged, so the `host-rules.json` parity fixtures keep their ids. `contracts.test.ts` builds rows from a long task title, a status headline and a failing check list, and validates the set and push against `NextTurnSet` and `NextTurnTrayPush`.

Fixed in 85ba54c1e8. When a Skip names a row that sits before the cursor (one New set already paged past), the cursor now moves back by one. Only the skipped row leaves the pool, and the rows on screen stay put. A test pins your sequence: New set, then a late Skip for Verify, leaves Review/Wrap up/Next step in view, and Undo skip brings Verify back to the front. I also fuzzed 4,000 random verb sequences offline against "a skip hides only its row, more drops only the last row, Undo skip brings its row into view". The fuzzer finds this bug without the fix and finds nothing with it.

discussion_comments.comment_body: Good catch. Both assertions now use `should(value)`, which fails on `undefined` instead of short-circuiting. Checked by mutation: with the proto-to-host converter dropping `annotations`, the round-trip test now fails.

Added a real-SDK case that aborts the request from inside the retry notice, while the wait is pending: the stream ends well under the backoff delay, no second fetch happens, no text is emitted, and no `sdk.error` is captured for the cancellation.

Fixed in 24f543400: each side is now read by its own mode (sideContents): gitlink sides render as 'Subproject commit <sha>', regular sides as blob contents, for commit and staged previews; the working side falls back to the file reader when a submodule was replaced by a file. The real-submodule test commits a submodule-to-file replacement and checks the new side shows the file's contents.

Valid, and fixed in 1690c40bf. I removed the cap. Each failure record is what stops its run from falling back to an earlier checkpoint, so failures now persist for the life of the session, as checkpoint history does. Covered by `keeps every failure so no failed run falls back to an earlier checkpoint` in `checkpoint-records.test.ts`; it fails if the cap is put back.

-// Converse request. They pin the reason for the adapter floor of 5.0.65:

+// Converse request. Together they pin the adapter floor:

+//   1. OpenAI models reached through inference profiles (`us.openai.*`,

+//      not the generic `reasoningConfig` that adapters before 5.0.65 emitted
+//      for any id they did not recognise (cline/cline#14451, vercel/ai#19403);
+//   2. models the adapter cannot classify get no reasoning fields at all,
+//      instead of a `reasoningConfig` Bedrock rejects for models without
+//      reasoning support — adapters before 5.0.96 sent it for every

+//   3. the families the adapter does classify keep their native shapes from
+//      the id alone even when the catalog does not list the model, so a
+//      catalog that lags a model launch never switches thinking off.

+// Cases that would only assert the adapter's translation for an id it
+// classifies belong to the adapter's own suite and are deliberately absent.

discussion_comments.comment_body: Intentional. That case exercised none of Cline's routing; it only pinned how `@ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock` translates an id it classifies itself, which belongs to the adapter's own suite. The remaining cases pin what goes through Cline's resolver, catalog lookup and portable-reasoning path, and the live run in the PR body records Nova 2 Lite's accepted request shape.
